headline: High-risk default interaction: Open Interpreter can read/write the shared filesystem and execute code, creating dangerous leakage, conflict, and cascading-error paths with Chatwoot’s customer-support data.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can expose customer messages and reports, while Open Interpreter can read the filesystem and clipboard by default. If Chatwoot outputs are copied or saved into shared files, Open Interpreter may treat attacker-controlled content as instructions. The pathway is plausible but not automatic, so medium fits better than low.
conditions: IF Chatwoot outputs are copied into a file or clipboard that Open Interpreter reads
IF Open Interpreter is run with default file access and no content provenance checks
mitigations: Keep Chatwoot exports out of shared folders
Disable clipboard bridging between the tools
Use separate OS users or profiles
Require manual review before Open Interpreter processes Chatwoot content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for copied artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages. Open Interpreter has broad filesystem read/write and broad network egress, so any shared workspace or copied export can be read and transmitted onward. That creates a realistic exfiltration path in default use, with sensitive data exposure and no built-in isolation by default.
conditions: IF Chatwoot exports or transcripts are placed on the local machine
IF Open Interpreter is allowed to read those files while network egress remains enabled
mitigations: Store Chatwoot data in a separate workspace
Disable Open Interpreter network egress for support-data sessions
Run Open Interpreter in an isolated container
Redact customer identifiers before any handoff
requires-engineering: enforce per-folder access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Open Interpreter can write the filesystem and modify git state, and its concurrency model shares state via filesystem. Chatwoot is a separate support system that can also produce reports and messages, so if both operate on the same directory or repo, concurrent writes can corrupt state or overwrite work. The overlap is dangerous by default once a shared workspace exists.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or git repository
IF Open Interpreter is used with write access while Chatwoot exports artifacts into that location
mitigations: Use distinct directories for each agent
Avoid letting Open Interpreter touch git repos containing Chatwoot exports
Pause one agent before the other writes shared files
Back up the workspace before any automation run
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can generate customer-facing content and reports, and Open Interpreter can execute shell commands and subprocesses. If Open Interpreter treats Chatwoot output as authoritative, it can turn a mistaken message or report into an irreversible action such as file edits or external API calls. The pair therefore has a strong default cascade from generated text to action-taking.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter consumes Chatwoot-generated text as instructions or facts
IF the resulting commands are executed without a human verification step
mitigations: Require human approval for every command derived from Chatwoot output
Separate factual extraction from action execution
Log and review all generated commands before running them
Use a read-only staging copy of Chatwoot output
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot handles customer data and interaction history, while Open Interpreter can access anything reachable on the local machine and send data to configured model providers. If regulated customer records are moved into Open Interpreter sessions, retention and residency controls may diverge from Chatwoot’s support workflow. The mismatch is plausible but not proven from the profiles alone, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated customer records are copied from Chatwoot into Open Interpreter sessions
IF the configured model provider stores prompts or logs outside the required residency boundary
mitigations: Keep regulated records out of Open Interpreter prompts
Use a provider with approved residency and retention terms
Minimize logs for support-data sessions
Document the data flow between systems
requires-engineering: implement retention and deletion controls
